questions.questionText: Your team needs to automatically generate a thumbnail image every time a user uploads a high-resolution photo to a Cloud Storage bucket. The processing logic is just a few lines of Python code. Which compute service is the most cost-effective and operationally simple choice for this event-driven task?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions is a lightweight, serverless compute service perfect for single-purpose, event-driven functions like responding to Cloud Storage upload events. It requires no infrastructure management and scales automatically.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine requires managing virtual machines, OS patching, and manual scaling setup, which is massive operational overhead for a simple event-driven script.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE requires provisioning and managing a container orchestration cluster, which is far too complex and costly for a simple thumbnail generator.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: While App Engine is a PaaS, the Flexible environment requires spinning up VMs under the hood and is not optimized for instantaneous, lightweight event-driven execution like Cloud Functions.

questions.questionText: You are deploying a stateless web application packaged as a Docker container. The application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes and long periods of zero traffic. You want a fully managed service that charges only when requests are being processed and can scale to zero. Which service should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed, serverless compute platform explicitly designed for deploying stateless containers. It automatically scales up based on incoming requests and natively scales down to zero when there is no traffic, ensuring cost optimization.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine runs continuously until manually stopped; it does not natively scale to zero based on HTTP traffic without complex custom scaling logic.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: GKE Standard requires a minimum baseline of node infrastructure to be running and does not scale entirely to zero out-of-the-box for web traffic.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine Flexible requires at least one instance to be running at all times and cannot scale to zero.

questions.questionText: Your enterprise company is migrating its on-premises data center to Google Cloud. You have hundreds of legacy applications running on VMware vSphere. The CIO has mandated a strict timeline, meaning there is no time to refactor the applications or change hypervisors. Which compute service should you select?

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud VMware Engine provides a fully managed VMware vSphere environment natively running in Google Cloud. It is explicitly designed for fast 'lift and shift' migrations of VMware workloads without the need to refactor, change tools, or modify the hypervisor.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Migrating to Compute Engine would require converting the VMware VMs to Compute Engine instances, which changes the hypervisor and tooling.
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: Bare Metal Solution provides raw physical servers, primarily for Oracle databases, and does not provide a managed VMware vSphere environment.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Migrating to GKE would require containerizing all the legacy applications, which heavily violates the requirement of 'no time to refactor'.

questions.questionText: A data science team runs nightly batch processing jobs that involve massive amounts of data computation. These jobs are fault-tolerant; if a server crashes, the job can simply be restarted from a checkpoint without data corruption. How can you minimize the compute costs for these workloads on Compute Engine?
options: Use Spot VMs for the compute instances.
Use Shielded VMs for the compute instances.
Use Sole-tenant nodes for the compute instances.
Use Confidential VMs for the compute instances.
correctAnswers: Use Spot VMs for the compute instances.

explanation.general explanation: Spot VMs (formerly preemptible VMs) are highly affordable compute instances that Google Cloud can reclaim at any time. They offer steep discounts compared to standard VMs and are the ideal choice for fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads like batch processing.

why other options are wrong.Use Shielded VMs for the compute instanc: Shielded VMs focus on verifiable integrity and rootkit defense, not cost optimization for batch jobs.
why other options are wrong.Use Sole-tenant nodes for the compute in: Sole-tenant nodes are dedicated physical servers for compliance or BYOL, and they typically increase costs.
why other options are wrong.Use Confidential VMs for the compute ins: Confidential VMs encrypt data in use (in memory). They provide enhanced security, not cost savings.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a legacy application that relies on deep OS kernel modifications and specific, non-standard networking configurations that cannot be supported in containerized or PaaS environments. Which Google Cloud compute service provides the necessary level of control?

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine provides Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS). It gives you complete, root-level control over the virtual machine, including the ability to run custom operating systems, modify the kernel, and implement custom networking configurations.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine is a PaaS that abstracts away low-level OS management; you cannot make deep kernel modifications.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is a serverless container platform that does not provide access to the underlying host OS or kernel.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): While you can customize nodes to some degree, running highly specific, non-standard kernel modifications for legacy apps is best suited for raw IaaS, not a container orchestrator.

questions.questionText: A developer has written a web application in Python 3.9 using the Flask framework. They do not know how to write Dockerfiles and do not want to manage containers or infrastructure. The app needs to automatically scale from zero to handle sudden bursts of traffic. Which service is the best fit?

explanation.general explanation: App Engine Standard is a fully managed PaaS that allows developers to deploy source code directly in supported languages (like Python) without managing Docker containers. It natively supports scaling to zero and rapid scaling for traffic spikes.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine Flexible requires managing a Dockerfile (either implicitly or explicitly) for custom runtimes, and it cannot scale down to zero.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run requires the application to be packaged into a Docker container, which the developer does not know how to do.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine requires full infrastructure management, OS patching, and manual scaling configurations.

questions.questionText: Your organization is moving towards a microservices architecture and wants to use Kubernetes. However, the operations team lacks experience in managing Kubernetes infrastructure, such as provisioning nodes, upgrading node OS, and configuring cluster scaling. Which service provides the Kubernetes API without the operational overhead of node management?

explanation.general explanation: GKE Autopilot is a mode of operations in GKE where Google fully manages the underlying node infrastructure, including provisioning, scaling, and security patching. You interact purely with the Kubernetes API to deploy pods, removing all node management overhead.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: GKE Standard requires you to configure and manage node pools, VM sizes, and cluster autoscaling.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run does not expose the full Kubernetes API; it is a simplified Knative-based service for stateless containers.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine with Microk8s: This approach requires managing the VMs, the OS, and installing and maintaining the Kubernetes distribution entirely yourself.

questions.questionText: You are designing an architecture for a set of new web APIs. To keep costs down in development environments, you require compute services that can scale down to exactly zero instances when not in use. Which two Google Cloud services provide this capability? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Both Cloud Run and Cloud Functions are serverless compute offerings on Google Cloud. They natively support scaling to zero when there are no incoming requests or events, ensuring you incur no compute charges during idle periods.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: VMs run continuously and incur costs until they are manually stopped or terminated.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: A GKE Standard cluster requires a minimum set of nodes to be running to maintain the cluster state, so it cannot scale to zero.
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: These are dedicated physical servers leased on a continuous basis; they do not scale up or down.

questions.questionText: Your company runs a massive, mission-critical Oracle database on-premises. Due to strict Oracle licensing constraints, the database must run on dedicated physical hardware that is not virtualized. You want to migrate this database to Google Cloud. Which compute option must you use?

explanation.general explanation: Bare Metal Solution provides purpose-built, dedicated physical servers housed in Google Cloud data centers. It is designed specifically to run specialized workloads like Oracle databases that require non-virtualized physical hardware for performance or strict licensing reasons.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Sole-tenant nodes: While Sole-tenant nodes are dedicated physical servers, the VMs running on them are still virtualized instances, which may violate strict non-virtualized licensing requirements.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Standard VMs: Standard VMs run on shared, virtualized infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud VMware Engine: This provides a virtualized VMware environment, which violates the requirement for non-virtualized physical hardware.

questions.questionText: You are designing an application that consists of 50 interdependent microservices. You require advanced traffic management, mutual TLS (mTLS) between services, and complex deployment strategies like canary releases using Anthos Service Mesh (Istio). Which compute platform should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: GKE provides the robust orchestration required for a massive microservices architecture. It natively integrates with Anthos Service Mesh (Istio) to provide advanced traffic management, security (mTLS), and observability across complex service topologies.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: While Cloud Run can handle microservices, it does not natively run Istio/Anthos Service Mesh for complex internal mTLS and advanced service mesh traffic routing rules.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine is a PaaS for web applications, lacking the deep orchestration and service mesh capabilities required for 50 complex microservices.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions is for simple event-driven snippets, not for orchestrating a complex, interconnected microservices architecture.

questions.questionText: An off-the-shelf software application has very specific resource requirements: it needs exactly 14 vCPUs and 50 GB of RAM. Using a standard predefined machine type would result in over-provisioning and wasted budget. How can you deploy this efficiently on Google Cloud?
options: Create a Compute Engine instance using a Custom Machine Type.
Deploy the application to Cloud Run and specify exact CPU and RAM limits.
Use App Engine Flexible with custom scaling parameters.
Provision a smaller Compute Engine instance and enable CPU bursting.
correctAnswers: Create a Compute Engine instance using a Custom Machine Type.

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine allows you to create Custom Machine Types. This lets you independently specify the exact number of vCPUs and the exact amount of memory needed for your workload, thereby optimizing costs by avoiding the over-provisioning inherent in fixed, predefined machine types.

why other options are wrong.Deploy the application to Cloud Run and: Cloud Run has maximum limits on CPU and RAM that are lower than 14 vCPUs and 50 GB, making it unsuitable for this monolithic software requirement.
why other options are wrong.Use App Engine Flexible with custom scal: App Engine Flexible does not allow you to define highly specific, custom vCPU-to-RAM ratios for individual instances in the way Custom Machine Types do.
why other options are wrong.Provision a smaller Compute Engine insta: Standard Compute Engine instances do not support arbitrary 'CPU bursting' beyond their provisioned limits (except for e2-micro/small, which do not scale to 14 vCPUs).

questions.questionText: Your development team has fully embraced containerization and packages all applications into custom Docker images. Which two Google Cloud compute services are specifically designed to natively run these custom container images? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run is built specifically to run stateless Docker containers in a serverless environment. GKE is a managed Kubernetes service explicitly designed to orchestrate and run containerized applications.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine Standard runs application source code in sandboxed, predefined runtimes; it does not allow you to bring your own custom Docker containers (that requires App Engine Flexible).
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: Bare Metal Solution provides raw physical servers, primarily for legacy databases, not a native environment for orchestrating Docker containers.

questions.questionText: You are building a lightweight web portal using Node.js. The application has a highly variable user base, with weeks of inactivity followed by sudden spikes. You want a fully managed environment where you only deploy your code and Google handles the rest, including scaling down to zero. Which service should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: App Engine Standard is a fully managed Platform as a Service (PaaS) ideal for web applications with variable traffic. It supports standard languages like Node.js natively, requires absolutely no infrastructure management, and scales to zero during periods of inactivity.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Requires full management of VMs, OS patching, and complex autoscaling setup. It does not scale to zero automatically.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Requires managing a Kubernetes cluster, which is excessive overhead for a simple Node.js web portal.
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: Provides physical servers for legacy databases, completely unsuitable for a modern, serverless web app.

questions.questionText: Your company currently runs an on-premises Kubernetes cluster for its containerized applications. You want to migrate to Google Cloud with the least amount of architectural changes and continue using your existing Helm charts and Kubernetes manifests. Which service should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: Migrating from an on-premises Kubernetes cluster to GKE provides the path of least resistance. GKE is a fully managed, conformant Kubernetes environment, meaning your existing manifests, Helm charts, and deployment pipelines will work with minimal changes.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: While Cloud Run runs containers, it uses a simplified Knative model. You would have to abandon your complex Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine Flex uses containers but is a PaaS, not a conformant Kubernetes environment.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Migrating to Compute Engine would mean manually installing and managing your own Kubernetes cluster on VMs, which defeats the purpose of moving to a managed cloud.

questions.questionText: You need to execute a simple data transformation script written in Node.js every time a new message is published to a specific Cloud Pub/Sub topic. The execution time is typically less than 2 seconds. What is the most appropriate and cost-effective compute service?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions is a serverless, event-driven compute service perfectly suited for executing lightweight code in response to Google Cloud events, such as a message arriving in a Pub/Sub topic. It scales automatically and charges only for the execution time.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Maintaining a continuous VM just to wait for Pub/Sub messages is an inefficient and costly over-provisioning of resources.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Creating a Kubernetes cluster for a simple 2-second script introduces massive operational overhead and unnecessary costs.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine Flexible instances are designed for continuous web serving, not lightweight, sub-second event-driven triggers.

questions.questionText: Spot VMs offer substantial discounts compared to standard Compute Engine instances, but they can be preempted by Google at any time. Which two scenarios are considered excellent, robust use cases for Spot VMs? (Choose two)
options: Stateless web servers placed behind a Cloud Load Balancer.
The primary master node of a highly available relational database.
An in-memory caching server (like Redis) requiring high uptime.
correctAnswers: Stateless web servers placed behind a Cloud Load Balancer.

explanation.general explanation: Spot VMs are ideal for stateless, fault-tolerant workloads. Batch rendering jobs can usually resume from a checkpoint if interrupted. Stateless web servers in a Managed Instance Group behind a load balancer can be preempted without dropping state, as the load balancer simply routes traffic to other healthy instances.

why other options are wrong.The primary master node of a highly avai: If a master database node is preempted, the database will go down, causing an outage.
Legacy systems are rarely fault-tolerant and abrupt preemptions would likely cause data corruption and severe downtime.
why other options are wrong.An in-memory caching server (like Redis): Preempting an in-memory cache drops all cached data, defeating its purpose and causing performance degradation.

questions.questionText: Your data science team needs to train a deep learning model. The training software requires specific NVIDIA GPUs, custom CUDA drivers, and a specific version of Ubuntu Linux. Which compute service provides the necessary hardware access and OS-level customization?

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine provides Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), granting you full control over the virtual machine. This allows you to attach specific hardware accelerators (GPUs), install custom OS kernels (like specific Ubuntu versions), and load custom hardware drivers (like CUDA).

why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: App Engine is a PaaS and does not allow for attaching specific GPUs or modifying the underlying host OS with custom CUDA drivers.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is a serverless platform for standard HTTP containers and does not support attaching GPUs for deep learning training.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions are for lightweight event execution and do not support GPU attachments.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a stateless, containerized e-commerce frontend. During flash sales, traffic can spike from zero to thousands of requests per second instantly. You need a serverless container platform that scales extremely fast and bills you strictly per request down to the millisecond. Which service should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed, serverless container platform that scales out almost instantaneously to handle massive traffic spikes and scales down to zero. It bills based on exact usage time and requests, making it perfect for volatile, containerized web workloads.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot: While GKE Autopilot manages nodes, it does not scale to zero or respond to instant flash-sale spikes as rapidly as Cloud Run.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine Standard is excellent for rapid scaling, but it runs source code in restricted runtimes, not arbitrary Docker containers.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Managed Instance Groups: VMs take significantly longer to boot (minutes) compared to Cloud Run containers (seconds or milliseconds), making them poorly suited for instant flash-sale spikes.

questions.questionText: You need to migrate an aging internal application that runs exclusively on Windows Server 2012. The application requires an attached persistent block storage drive and relies on a static internal IP address. Which service is required for this migration?

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine provides Virtual Machines (IaaS) that natively support Windows Server operating systems, persistent block storage (Persistent Disks), and static internal IP configurations required by legacy monolithic applications.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine does not run Windows Server; it supports specific programming language runtimes on Linux.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run runs stateless Linux containers, not legacy Windows Server monolithic applications with attached block storage.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): While GKE can run Windows containers, an aging legacy app on Windows Server 2012 generally requires a full VM, not a containerized environment.

questions.questionText: Your company handles highly regulated financial data. A new compliance mandate dictates that certain workloads must run on physical hardware that is completely dedicated to your organization and not shared with any other cloud tenants. Which two compute options fulfill this strict hardware isolation requirement? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Sole-tenant nodes provide dedicated Compute Engine physical servers where only your VMs run. Bare Metal Solution provides dedicated, non-virtualized physical servers. Both ensure that no other Google Cloud customers share the underlying physical hardware, satisfying strict compliance isolation requirements.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot: GKE Autopilot runs on shared, multi-tenant Google Cloud infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is a serverless platform that runs on shared, multi-tenant infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine runs on shared, multi-tenant Google Cloud infrastructure.

questions.questionText: You have a web application packaged as a custom Docker container. The application needs to process some background web requests that take up to 30 minutes to complete. You want a managed App Engine environment, but App Engine Standard has a strict timeout limit for HTTP requests. Which service should you use?

explanation.general explanation: App Engine Flexible runs custom Docker containers on Compute Engine VMs under the hood. It supports longer request timeouts (up to 24 hours) compared to App Engine Standard, making it suitable for longer-running web requests while still providing managed PaaS features.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions has a strict maximum timeout of 9 minutes (or up to 60 mins for 2nd gen in specific cases), but the requirement asks for a managed App Engine environment.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine is raw IaaS, completely lacking the managed PaaS features requested.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE is a container orchestrator requiring cluster management, not a managed App Engine PaaS environment.

questions.questionText: You are planning a new application and want to use Kubernetes for orchestration. However, you want to pay only for the CPU and memory resources that your application pods actually request, rather than paying for the underlying worker nodes' capacity. Which service mode achieves this?

explanation.general explanation: In GKE Autopilot, Google manages the node infrastructure. You are billed purely for the vCPU, memory, and disk resources requested by your scheduled Pods, completely eliminating the cost of unused capacity on underlying worker nodes.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: In GKE Standard, you pay for the underlying Compute Engine VMs (worker nodes) regardless of how many pods are scheduled on them.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is not Kubernetes; it is a serverless platform. The question specifically requires Kubernetes orchestration.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine involves paying for full VMs, not per-pod resource requests.

questions.questionText: Your company holds existing 'Bring Your Own License' (BYOL) agreements for Microsoft SQL Server. The licensing terms require you to license the software based on the physical cores of the underlying server. How can you deploy these licenses compliantly on Google Cloud?
options: Deploy the VMs on Compute Engine Sole-tenant nodes.
Deploy the VMs using Compute Engine Custom Machine Types.
Deploy the database using Cloud SQL.
Deploy the VMs using Spot VMs.
correctAnswers: Deploy the VMs on Compute Engine Sole-tenant nodes.

explanation.general explanation: Sole-tenant nodes provide dedicated physical servers for your workloads, offering visibility into the underlying physical hardware. This allows you to map VMs to physical cores, which is necessary to comply with per-physical-core BYOL licensing agreements from vendors like Microsoft.

why other options are wrong.Deploy the VMs using Compute Engine Cust: Custom Machine Types run on shared physical hardware, preventing you from tying licenses to specific physical cores.
Cloud SQL is a fully managed service where Google handles the licensing; you cannot use physical-core BYOL licenses here.
Spot VMs are temporary instances on shared hardware and do not support physical-core BYOL compliance.

questions.questionText: You are tasked with designing an architecture that minimizes operational overhead. The CTO has mandated the use of 'serverless' compute services where all underlying infrastructure provisioning, OS patching, and capacity planning are completely hidden from the developers. Which two services meet this definition? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run and Cloud Functions are true serverless compute offerings. They fully abstract away the underlying infrastructure, requiring zero OS management, security patching, or manual scaling capacity configurations from the user.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine is IaaS; you must manage the OS, patching, and scaling manually.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: GKE Standard requires you to configure and manage node pools and cluster scaling.
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: Bare Metal provides physical servers requiring complete manual management of the OS and infrastructure.

questions.questionText: Every time a new customer signs up, a document is created in your Firestore database. You need a small snippet of code to execute automatically upon document creation to send a welcome email via a third-party API. What is the most lightweight compute service for this task?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions natively integrates with Firebase and Google Cloud event triggers, including Firestore document creations. It is the most lightweight, serverless way to run a short snippet of code in response to a specific database event.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: While Cloud Run could handle events via Eventarc, it requires packaging the code into a Docker container, adding unnecessary overhead for a simple code snippet.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine is designed for full web applications, not lightweight, single-purpose event-driven snippets.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Managing a VM to run a tiny script triggered by a database is massive operational overkill.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to process 10,000 independent images every night. The processing logic is packaged in a Docker container, and each image takes about 5 minutes to process. You want a fully managed, serverless solution to run these containers in parallel without managing a Kubernetes cluster. Which service is best suited for this?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run Jobs allows you to execute a containerized script or tool that runs to completion. It is specifically designed to execute parallel arrays of independent tasks (like processing thousands of images) in a fully managed, serverless environment without needing to provision a cluster.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions is optimized for short-lived, event-driven triggers, not orchestrating 10,000 5-minute containerized batch tasks.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine handles HTTP requests, not background containerized batch jobs running to completion.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine would require you to manually provision VMs, schedule the tasks, and manage the execution, which is not a managed serverless solution.

questions.questionText: You are deploying a High Performance Computing (HPC) workload for weather forecasting. The application is highly CPU-bound and requires ultra-low latency networking between nodes. Which Compute Engine machine family should you select?

explanation.general explanation: The Compute-optimized machine family (like C2/C3) is designed specifically for high-performance computing (HPC), electronic design automation (EDA), and other highly CPU-bound workloads. They offer the highest performance per core and support compact placement policies for ultra-low latency networking.

why other options are wrong.Memory-optimized (M2/M3) machine family: These are built for large in-memory databases (like SAP HANA), not primarily for CPU-bound HPC workloads.
why other options are wrong.General-purpose (E2) machine family: These offer a balance of price and performance for standard web servers, lacking the extreme CPU power and low latency required for HPC.
why other options are wrong.Shared-core machine family: These are small, burstable instances for microservices, entirely unsuited for HPC.

questions.questionText: While managed services abstract away infrastructure, some Google Cloud compute services operate as Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), making you responsible for applying OS security patches and managing the operating system lifecycle. Which two services require this level of administration? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine (virtual machines) and Bare Metal Solution (physical servers) are IaaS offerings. While Google manages the underlying physical infrastructure and virtualization layer, you (the customer) are completely responsible for managing the guest operating system, including patching and security updates.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Google manages the entire OS and infrastructure stack.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: Google manages the PaaS environment, OS, and runtimes.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Google manages the serverless execution environment and underlying OS.

questions.questionText: You need to migrate an older 3-tier application (Web, Application, and Database tiers) to Google Cloud. The application components communicate via specific static IP addresses and rely on an older Linux kernel. To ensure a successful migration with zero code changes, which compute service should you use?

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine (VMs) is the most appropriate choice for a strict 'lift and shift' migration of a legacy multi-tier application. It allows you to replicate the exact OS kernel, complex network topology, and static IP configurations of the on-premises environment.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Requires refactoring the application into containers and adopting Kubernetes networking, violating the 'zero code changes' and specific static IP requirements.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: Is a PaaS designed for web applications, not for hosting a 3-tier legacy architecture with custom kernels.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Is a serverless platform for stateless containers, unsuited for a legacy 3-tier monolithic migration.

questions.questionText: Your development team wants to deploy a simple Go-based webhook listener that receives HTTP POST requests from a third-party payment gateway. The listener code is stored in a Cloud Source Repository. They want a serverless deployment directly from the source code without building Docker containers themselves. Which service is the most straightforward choice?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions allows you to deploy simple, single-purpose HTTP endpoints directly from source code (like Go, Python, or Node.js). Google Cloud automatically builds the container behind the scenes and manages the serverless deployment, making it extremely straightforward for webhook listeners.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Requires manually setting up a VM, installing Go, and configuring a web server, which is neither serverless nor straightforward.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Requires the developers to build Docker containers and manage Kubernetes manifests, explicitly violating the requirement.
why other options are wrong.Bare Metal Solution: Provides physical servers, which is the exact opposite of a simple serverless deployment.
